proof_summary: The proof writes the valuation as \(\sum_{i\ge1}(q_i^2-S(q_i))\), where \(q_i=\lfloor N/p^i\rfloor\) and \(S(q)=\sum_{k=1}^q k\lfloor q/k\rfloor\), by counting pairs divisible by \(p^i\) in the gcd product and using the factorial valuation formula for the denominator (with \(S(q)\le q^2\) also proving exact divisibility). For \(N=np+k\) with \(0\le k<p\), every quotient \(\lfloor(np+k)/p^i\rfloor\) for \(i\ge1\) equals \(\lfloor np/p^i\rfloor\), so the valuation formula is unchanged.
